query: Foragers at the Back Door {At Pell's back door a forager in muddy boots is waiting to sell the morning's haul from the Whisperwood. She catches your eye. "Cheaper than the counter, love. No questions."|The forager at the back door again, basket heavier, prices lower. She remembers you.|The back-door forager nods at you like an old business partner. Today's basket has something in it that's still moving.} {The basket smells of moss and rain.|There's moonpetal in it, wrapped in a dock leaf.|{season == "winter": Her fingers are blue with cold.|Old Pell can be heard counting aloud inside.}} Buy straight from her basket {You buy a bundle of roots for half the counter price and spend the evening sorting the useful from the merely muddy.|You buy the moonpetal, dock leaf and all. It's the real thing; you can tell by the way it doesn't wilt.|You buy the moving thing, which turns out to be a root that wriggles toward water. You learn a great deal keeping it alive.} Ask where she found it all {She tells you about a clearing west of the stream where the moss glows. You write it down and do not go there, yet.|She tells you which mushrooms lie about being safe. It's an education, and it's free.|She tells you, lowering her voice, about a stream that runs uphill on nights of the full moon. Then she laughs and says it's probably nothing.}
